summary: Research exact DQC rule semantics (XULE source) and FinMR dataset construction to push Task 3 accuracy to ~99%

verified_from_source: SOURCE FILES: DataQualityCommittee/dqc_us_rules (master), cloned to /tmp/claude-1000/dqc/dqc_us_rules. Rule: dqc_us_rules/source/us/2026/DQC_0126.xule (120 lines). Once whitespace and line endings are ignored, the 2023, 2024 and 2025 copies have the same logic; the only differences are the taxonomy header and one comment line. The dataset filings use dei/us-gaap 2026 namespaces, so the 2026 ruleset applies. Constants are in source/us/2026/constant.xule and functions in source/us/2026/functions.xule. There is no docs/DQC_US_0126 folder; docs/DQC_IFRS_0126/DQC_0126.md holds the shared rule description and a US example message.

WHICH NETWORKS QUALIFY (DQC_0126.xule:30-34, constant.xule:144 and :208-229). The rule loops over PRESENTATION networks (parent-child) whose role definition contains the exact, case-sensitive text '- Statement -'. It drops a network if the LOWER-CASED role URI contains any of: parenthetical, equity, deficit, stockholders, capital, investment, change, shareholder, convertible, preferred, temporaryequity, redeemable, netproceedsfromallsources, membersinterest, membershipinterest, highlights, employee, ebp. It also drops a network if the lower-cased role DEFINITION contains 'schedule iii', 'schedule iv' or 'net worth'. The 2023 version lacks 'employee' and 'ebp'.

CUBE SKIP (DQC_0126.xule:28-33, constant.xule:177-195). A presentation role is skipped when its URI is the drs-role of any STATEMENT_CUBE, i.e. a definition-linkbase hypercube in a role whose definition contains '- Statement -'. That cube list has its own URI exclusions: parenthetical, equity, deficit, stockholders, capital, investment, changes, shareholder, convertible, preferred, temporaryequity, redeemable, netproceedsfromallsources, membersinterest; plus 'schedule iii'/'schedule iv' in the definition, and a few investment-schedule tables. Comment at line 31: the rule does not run when the statement is a table, because rule 118 handles that. So any statement with dimensions is skipped entirely.

CALC NETWORK = SAME ROLE URI as the presentation role (DQC_0126.xule:36 and :47). The concepts checked ($calcNetworkSource) are the set of SOURCE (parent) concepts of all summation-item relationships in that role. For each parent, $calcComponents are its DIRECT summation-item children in that role, with their weights. It is one level only, with no recursion into grandchildren; every parent is checked on its own using the reported values of its direct children.

FS DECIMALS (DQC_0126.xule:38-39, functions.xule:934-953). fs_decimals = most_frequent(decimals of [nonils covered @concept in $calcNetworkSource]). The square brackets mean NON-DIMENSIONAL facts only; 'covered' means all periods and units are included; only PARENT concepts count, not leaf children. most_frequent builds a dict keyed by count, so on a tie the last value in set iteration order wins.

TOTAL FACT (DQC_0126.xule:80-85). For a duration concept: the non-dimensional, non-nil fact with period.start = DocumentPeriodEndDate context start, period.end = that context end, AND decimals == fs_decimals. For an instant concept: period end = that context end, AND decimals == fs_decimals. The document period comes from first(list({covered @concept.local-name='DocumentPeriodEndDate'})).period (lines 21-23). '@@' keeps period aligned (XULE doc lines 927-944), so addends align to the same period. If no total with decimals == fs_decimals exists, the rule does not fire (the SGU test log shows only 1 firing for a whole filing, so prior-period alignments do not fire).

ADDENDS (DQC_0126.xule:50-58). For each child, in calc-arc order: first-value( [nonils @concept=child where decimals == fs_decimals] * weight , first(list([... where decimals >= fs_decimals])) * weight , first(list([... where decimals < fs_decimals])) * weight ). All factsets are square-bracket (NON-DIMENSIONAL ONLY, XULE doc lines 400-414). Period, unit and entity stay uncovered, so children must share the total's period AND UNIT (implicit matching, doc lines 904-944). Unbound times weight gives unbound (XuleProcessor.evaluate_mult lines 1849-1850); first-value returns 'unbound' when every tier is empty (XuleFunctions.func_first_value lines 981-1009). $addend = sum(list), $addendNumber = count(list). If $addend is none the rule skips (lines 88-89), so with no children found it does not fire.

TOLERANCE (DQC_0126.xule:95, functions.xule:163-207). It calls tolerance_for_decimals($sum2, $addend, $addendNumber + 1). left_decimal = total.decimals (INF when none). right_decimal = $addend.decimals, or left_decimal when that is none. $addend is a computed value: weight multiplication creates a new XuleValue with no fact (evaluate_mult 1866-1868), and property_decimals returns none for non-facts (XuleProperties.py:2094-2098). So right_decimal = left_decimal, which makes d = the TOTAL's decimals (= fs_decimals). Tolerance = 10^(-d) * (n_found + 1), or 0 when d is INF. The rule FIRES only if abs(round(total, d) - round(addend, d)) > tolerance, a strict '>'.

OTHER SKIP (DQC_0126.xule:91-93). The rule skips if a child is LiabilitiesSubjectToCompromise AND a ReorganizationUnderChapter11OfUSBankruptcyCodeDisclosureTextBlock fact exists. That text occurs 0 times in dev and test. applicable_form (functions.xule:1031-1035) also gates by form type.

MESSAGE NUMBERS (DQC_0126.xule:98-112). 'The value of the concept {$concept_item} of {$sum2}' is the reported total, so gold extracted_value = $sum2. 'The sum of these child components is {$addend}' is the WEIGHTED sum of the children found, so gold calculated_value = $addend. The itemised $addend_string (lines 61-76) prints UNWEIGHTED child values, sorted by concept, with a '+' or '-' sign taken from the weight. Checked by hand on the IFRS doc example (the weighted sum gives 117,309,000) and on the SGU US test log (46-9-633+167+432-195 = -192 thousand, matching 'The sum ... is -192,000').

EMPIRICAL CHECK with a faithful scratch emulator (/tmp/claude-1000/dqc/work/x126.py, comparison script cmp.py). On DEV, the emulator fires on exactly 464 of our 465 '0126' predictions. That equals the official per_dqc n=464 for DQC_US_0126. Our calculated_value equals the emulator's $addend on 463 of the 464. It fires on none of our 0015/0117 predictions. On TEST, it fires on all 464 '0126' predictions with identical sums, plus 1 case we routed to 0015 (TEST3_000128). On the untruncated public_dev 0126 cases, emulator $addend = gold on 83 of 86; the 3 misses are truncation, plus DEV_000273 where the gold '320002' looks like a typo for 32002.

In every dev and test case where the emulator fires, the target period ends at the latest context end, except 6 cases that have later subsequent-event contexts. Each case has exactly one qualifying role, all calc roles have a matching presentation role, and there are no duplicate or prohibited calc arcs. 113 of the 464 dev firings have children with no fact; these are dropped, which matches our treatment of missing children as zero.

discrepancies_with_our_code: 1. UNIT NOT ALIGNED (rules.py:77, calc_children_sum). We sum the first non-dimensional fact of each child whatever its unitRef. XULE only uses child facts with the same unit as the total. This changes the calculated value on DEV3_000542 (we give 8790814; the rule gives 8412814). No test case is affected (all 464 test sums match the emulator).

2. CHILD FACT CHOICE IGNORES DECIMALS (rules.py:77-80). We take vals[0], the first fact in instance order. XULE uses three tiers: the fact with decimals == fs_decimals, then the first with decimals >= fs_decimals, then the first with decimals < fs_decimals. fs_decimals is the most frequent decimals among non-dimensional facts of the role's PARENT concepts across all periods. This only changes values when duplicate child facts disagree (for example a -3 fact and a -5 rounded fact). No current dev/test 0126 case is affected, but it is a latent risk.

3. TOTAL FACT CHOICE IGNORES DECIMALS (rules.py:58-64, reported()). XULE's $sum2 is the non-dimensional total whose decimals == fs_decimals; we take the first one. If no total has decimals == fs_decimals, XULE does not fire at all. Three test cases (TEST3_000097/165/166) have inconsistent duplicate totals (for example 3979000 at -3 and 4000000.0 at -5). Those are 0015/0117 predictions, not 0126, but the same first-fact choice is used for extraction there.

4. ROLE SCOPE (rules.py:71-73). We use EVERY calc role in which the target is a parent. XULE requires: (a) the calc role URI equals a presentation role URI; (b) that role's definition contains '- Statement -' and the URI and definition pass the exclusion lists; (c) the role is not a statement-cube drs-role. Our is_statement_role/calc_role_titles (rules.py:194-214) is not used in decide() and is looser anyway. It accepts ' statement ' in the title, checks only equity, stockholders, shareholders and 'changes in', and falls back to the role URI. This changes the decision on DEV3_000215 (cube role; XULE does not fire, we predict 0126).

5. FIRING TEST IS EXACT INEQUALITY (solve.py:363, 'if total != rep'). XULE fires only if |round(T,d) - round(S,d)| > 10^(-d) * (n_found + 1), where d = the total's decimals and INF gives exact comparison. With today's data no case falls inside the tolerance band (minimum ratio 1.18). Still, a filing with small rounding differences would be sent to 0126 by our code when XULE would not fire, so the case would fall through to m117_any or 0015_unlisted instead.

6. ROLE CHOICE AMONG SEVERAL (solve.py:362, max by found/total ratio). XULE emits one message per qualifying role, iterating $STATEMENT_PRES_NETWORKS.sort, and nothing in the rule picks one. Every dev and test case has exactly one qualifying role, so there is no current impact. Filtering to qualifying roles (item 4) makes this moot in practice.

7. sums filter 'x[2] > 0' (solve.py:359) matches XULE: no children found gives $addend none and the rule skips. Missing children treated as zero also matches. The weighted sum and the meaning of the reported number ($addend, the weighted sum) also match. Non-dimensional-only children (period_facts dims=False) match the square-bracket factsets.

8. PRIORITY OVERLAP (solve.py:380-385). in15 plus a negative reported value takes precedence over 0126. On TEST3_000128 the XULE 0126 rule also fires (total -4877, weighted children sum 5271) while we answer 0015. Dev has no case where both fire, so I have no evidence on which rule the dataset assigns here. Flagging it only.
recommended_changes: A. In Case.calc_children_sum (rules.py:67-83), pass the target total fact's unitRef and keep only child facts with f.unit == total.unit. Expected to fix DEV3_000542 (8790814 becomes 8412814), likely the only genuine 0126 calculated-value error.

B. Compute fs_decimals per calc role. Use the decimals of all non-dimensional, non-empty facts of every PARENT concept (arc 'from') in that role, any period; read 'INF' as infinity. Take the most frequent value; on a tie, take the last one in first-seen order (this approximates XULE's dict overwrite). Choose the total as the first non-dimensional target-period fact with decimals == fs_decimals, falling back to the first fact. Choose each child's value as: first fact with dec == fsd, else first with dec >= fsd, else first with dec < fsd, all within the same unit and period.

C. Restrict 0126 roles to: calc role URI that is also in the presentation linkbase; roleType definition contains '- Statement -' (case-sensitive); lower-cased URI contains none of [parenthetical, equity, deficit, stockholders, capital, investment, change, shareholder, convertible, preferred, temporaryequity, redeemable, netproceedsfromallsources, membersinterest, membershipinterest, highlights, employee, ebp]; lower-cased definition contains none of ['schedule iii', 'schedule iv', 'net worth']. Also skip the role if the definition linkbase has a definitionLink for the same role URI containing an arcrole/all (hypercube) arc, using cube exclusions [parenthetical, equity, deficit, stockholders, capital, investment, changes, shareholder, convertible, preferred, temporaryequity, redeemable, netproceedsfromallsources, membersinterest] on the URI. A drop-in reference implementation is in /tmp/claude-1000/dqc/work/x126.py (functions stmt_ok, cube_roles, run). This removes the wrong 0126 call on DEV3_000215, which then needs the 0117/0015 path.

D. Replace 'total != rep' (solve.py:363) with the XULE test. Let d = decimals of the chosen total (= fs_decimals; INF means tolerance 0 and exact compare) and n = number of children found. Fire iff abs(round_half_even(T, d) - round_half_even(S, d)) > Decimal(10) ** (-d) * (n + 1). Round with Decimal: q = 10**(-d); round(x/q)*q, using a high-precision context, because some filings carry decimals like 128.
E. Report calculated_value = the unrounded weighted sum S (XULE's {$addend}) and extracted_value = the chosen total's raw value. The current behaviour already does this.

F. Validate after the change by running /tmp/claude-1000/dqc/work/cmp.py (dev) and cmp_test.py (test). Target result: the emulator fires on exactly 464 dev cases, our sums match on all 464, and nothing changes on test except possibly TEST3_000128, which has no dev evidence either way, so leave its priority unchanged unless other evidence appears.

verified_from_source: SOURCE FILES. The rule is dqc_us_rules/source/us/2026/DQC_0117.xule (v29, cloned to /tmp/claude-1000/q117/dqc_us_rules). It has two assertions: US.0117.9574 (lines 11-161) and US.0117.10093 (lines 163-274), plus the function CheckSubTotalExists (lines 279-291). The helper tolerance_for_decimals_comp is in source/lib/functions.xule:209-245. The cube constants are in source/us/2026/constant.xule: STATEMENT_CUBES at 177-194, STATEMENT_PARENTHETICAL_CUBES at 196-197, NOTES_CUBES at 420. I checked engine behaviour against the XULE processor source (github.com/xbrlus/xule, plugin/xule/XuleProcessor.py, XuleValue.py, XuleModelIndexer.py). I also ran the real XULE engine (Arelle 2.46.1 + XULE 3.0.30055) on a synthetic taxonomy and instance with a trimmed copy of the rule (/tmp/claude-1000/q117/t/r0117.xule, inst.xml).

STATEMENT CUBE (constant.xule:177-194). A cube counts only if its drs-role definition contains '- Statement -' and its role URI, lower-cased, contains none of: parenthetical, equity, deficit, stockholders, capital, investment, changes, shareholder, convertible, preferred, temporaryequity, redeemable, netproceedsfromallsources, membersinterest. The definition also must not contain 'schedule iii' or 'schedule iv', and the cube concept must not be ScheduleOfInvestmentsTable or one of the other investment tables listed there. NOTES_CUBES are cubes whose definition contains '- Disclosure -'.

AXES (DQC_0117.xule:38). The axis local-name must be one of: StatementClassOfStockAxis, ProductOrServiceAxis, PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis, LongtermDebtTypeAxis, RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis, StatementBusinessSegmentsAxis, LimitedPartnersCapitalAccountByClassAxis, PartnerTypeOfPartnersCapitalAccountAxis, FiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsByMajorClassAxis, FinancialInstrumentAxis, InformationByCategoryOfDebtSecurityAxis. Only the local name is compared. The rule loops over every statement cube and every listed axis of that cube's hypercube.

WHICH FACTS ARE IN A CUBE (XuleValue.py:1511-1559, XuleModelIndexer.py:225-235). A fact is in a drs-role's cube when all of these hold: (1) its concept is a primary item of that role; (2) for every cube dimension, either its member is one of that dimension's usable members in the role, or it lacks the dimension and the dimension-default member is among those members; (3) for a closed hypercube, it has no dimension outside the cube. So a non-dimensional fact is in the cube only if every cube axis has a dimension-default.

SQUARE-BRACKET FACTSETS ARE CLOSED (xule_grammar.py:368-380; XuleProcessor.py:2807-2811). A [...] factset drops any fact that has a dimension not named in the filter. As a result, in 9574 the total ([... @$dim in $domain], line 74) is the fact with NO dimensions at all. Each member fact ([... @$dim = $member], line 93) has exactly one dimension, $dim. Facts that carry another axis besides the checked one are never summed and never used as the total in 9574. Unnamed aspects (concept, period, unit, entity) align implicitly: aggregates such as list() and sum() group by alignment (XuleProcessor.py:4383-4459). So every comparison is per concept + period + unit. Engine test: a slice X1 with a single-dim value of 30 against member×X1 facts summing to 24 was NOT flagged by 9574.

DOMAIN AND DEFAULT. $domain is the set of dimension-domain targets (line 41). fix_for_default_member (XuleProcessor.py:4948-4990) turns the default member into 'no dimension', so the total is the non-dimensional fact.

MEMBERS AND NESTING (lines 39, 84, 88-93). $members are ALL dimensional descendants of the axis in that drs-role, at every level. $member_descendants is that set minus the domain. A member is skipped when any of its domain-member ancestors (excluding the domain) has a single-dim fact for the same concept, period and unit. Otherwise its single-dim fact is summed. Effect: the highest reported level is summed, and a child is summed only when its parent has no fact. Members not declared under the axis in the statement role are never summed. Engine tests: default 100, A=60, A1 (child of A)=40, B=40 does not fire. Default 100, A1=40, B=40 with no A fires with 100 vs 80. Practice DEV_000142 agrees: gold calc 1,044,000 = 487k + 557k; the undeclared UnallocatedAndOtherSegmentsMember (99k) is excluded.

9574 GATES (lines 49-62, 65-67, 71, 76-81, 86). (a) SubTotalExists: take the in-cube monetary facts with $dim and more than one dimension (covered-dims, so still per concept+period). Every $dim member that appears in them must also have a single-dim in-cube fact; otherwise 9574 is skipped for that concept+period. Engine test confirmed. (b) No single-dim $dim facts for the concept+period in any parenthetical statement cube (added in v24.0.3). (c) Either no single-dim $dim facts exist in any Disclosure cube, or max(those facts) > TotalDefault. Engine test: default 25 with members 10 and 20, also in a note cube, is skipped; default 15 with members 10 and 20 in a note cube fires.

PERIOD (lines 30-31, 74). The total must satisfy period.days == 0 (instant) or period.days == the duration of the first dei:DocumentType fact's context. days = (end+1 day) - start, i.e. a day count that includes both endpoints (XuleProperties.py:954-960), and the match must be exact. Quarterly facts in a 10-K are never checked. A prior-year comparative with a different day count (e.g. FY2024 = 366 days vs FY2025 = 365) is never checked. Engine test confirmed. Members have no period filter, but the period alignment ties them to the total's period.

TOLERANCE (functions.xule:209-245). min_decimals is the minimum decimals over the member facts. INF or a value above 5 becomes 5. member_sums is not a fact, so its decimals are none and it takes min_decimals. tol = min(that, TotalDefault.decimals). The rule fires iff abs(round(sum, tol) - round(total, tol)) > 2*10^(-tol), using Python round, i.e. half-even (XuleProperties.py:1760-1780). If $right == none it is treated as 0 inside the function.

REVENUE EXCEPTIONS (lines 114-134). They apply only when TotalDefault.name is RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax or ...IncludingAssessedTax AND $dim == srt:ProductOrServiceAxis. Case 1: the statement cube's primary concepts include NoninterestIncome. Then it fires only if out of tolerance AND member_sums > TotalDefault. Case 2: otherwise, if member_sums < TotalDefault and the cube contains Revenues, it does NOT fire when the Revenues summation-item descendants in the cube's role have more than one element and include a RevenueFromContract... element. Otherwise it applies the normal tolerance test.

MESSAGE AND GOLD (lines 143-154; FinAuditing paper arXiv 2510.08886, sections 3.2.1 and 3.3.1). The gold comes from official XBRL US filing-results DQC messages, parsed by GPT-4o-mini. 9574 message: 'the concept {$TotalDefault.name} with a value of {$TotalDefault} is not equal to the dimensional breakdown of {$member_sums}'. So gold extracted = the non-dimensional total and gold calculated = member_sums. The FinMR practice gold agrees: every 0117 practice case whose facts survive the truncation has extracted = the non-dim fact and calc = the single-dim member sum. All 12 practice gold-'0' cases with visible facts have a reported 0-valued fact, as in the doc's PreferredStockValue example.

10093 = SECOND-AXIS CHECK (lines 163-274; this is how extra-dimension slices are handled). Take the in-cube facts with exactly 2 dims, one of them $dim. For each SubMember of $dim among them: Dim2 = first(other axis), which is arbitrary if there are several. Skip if Dim2 is LegalEntityAxis. CheckSubTotalExists: every Dim2 member that appears in 3+-dim facts with (SubMember, Dim2) needs a 2-dim (SubMember, Dim2-member) fact. Notes gate: closed 2-dim facts in Disclosure cubes, with the same max > total rule. TotalDefault = the SINGLE-dim fact $dim=SubMember (same period filter), and it must exist. member_facts = ALL 2-dim facts (SubMember, any Dim2 member), with no nesting dedup and no declared-member restriction beyond being in the cube. The message reports the dimensional total. Engine tests: total A=10 against A×X1=4 plus A×X2=1 gives 'total=10 sum=5 Dimensions: ProductOrServiceAxis=AMember'. Nested Dim2 members are all added (A×X1 6 + A×X1a 3 + A×X2 4 = 13 vs 10).

ENGINE QUIRK. In multi-concept instances 10093 fired for at most one concept per SubMember, and which one varied between runs. The output is also not deterministic unless --xule-ordered-iterations is set. So 10093 messages are rarer and arbitrary.

MISSING DEFAULT IN THE CURRENT ENGINE. With no non-dim fact, the factset yields 'unbound', and the current engine does NOT fire 9574 (tested with both the v29 rule and the Jan-2023 rule; also for the quarterly period and the note-cube variants). Inside tolerance_for_decimals_comp an unbound argument propagates (XuleProcessor.py:755, 1653, 2054-2120, 4285-4290).

RULE HISTORY (GitHub API). The v21 commit 65f4141583 (2023-07-27) added SubTotalExists, the notes gate and 10093. The parenthetical gate was added in v24.0.3 (e575b096b1, 2024-08-09). The Jan-2023 version dd2537bafc has none of these. Since v21 the 9574 logic is otherwise unchanged.

What that means: every numeric (@unit=*), non-nil fact of a listed concept with value strictly < 0 is tested. Zero and nil never fire. All periods and units are in scope (shares, pure and USD alike), so a discount rate stored as -0.0558 fires.

No dimension-count limit. A non-dimensional fact always fires if negative. A fact with ANY number of dimensions fires unless one of four exclusions matches: (a) any EXPLICIT member's lower-cased local name contains a listed substring (functions.xule 454-457, explicit members only); (b) any explicit member qname is in the member list; (c) any axis, typed or explicit, is in the axis list; (d) the fact has an axis from the axis-member list carrying one of its listed members (functions.xule 470-486).
Matching is by qname, not local name: the member, axis and axis-member lists are us-gaap/srt qnames (constant-us-gaap.xule 226, 235-238, 253). Only the substring test (a) works on local names.

Substring list (constant-us-gaap.xule 206-209 plus the rules taxonomy, allowableSubString reference): adjust, consolidat, eliminat, netting, reconcili, reclass, basisswap, unfunded. In 2023-2026 'basisswap' and 'unfunded' are also hard-coded. The 2022 taxonomy list has no 'unfunded'.

One message per qualifying fact. Nothing in the rule makes one negative fact suppress another: no choice between a headline and its members, no dimension-count preference, no first-only logic. The only collapse is XULE's fact-index de-duplication (XuleModelIndexer.py 77-108): facts with identical aspects (concept, period, unit, entity, every dimension) and equal decimals-rounded values become one, keeping the more precise. Identical-aspect facts with DIFFERENT values are all kept and each fires.

Emission order is undefined. The fact index and pre-matched factsets are Python sets of ModelFacts (XuleModelIndexer.py 50-121; XuleProcessor.py factset_pre_match 2505-2690), and process_filtered_facts iterates them (XuleProcessor.py 2757). The xule source itself (ordered_iteration docstring, XuleProcessor.py ~2726-2747) says these sets are hashed by identity, so iteration follows memory addresses, is not reproducible between runs, and PYTHONHASHSEED does not help. Only the optional --xule-ordered-iterations flag sorts by objectIndex (document load order).

verified_from_source: THE KEY SOURCE IS THE ORGANIZERS' OWN CONSTRUCTION CODE. It is in github.com/The-FinAI/XBRL_Auditing ('Gold-answer extraction from XBRL DQC messages, companion code for FinAuditing'), cloned to /tmp/claude-1000/finaud/XBRL_Auditing. The useful files: mathematical_reasoning_{0015,0117,0126}.ipynb; input_files/mathematical_reasoning_{0015,0117,0126}.csv, which hold the raw DQC messages; agentic_benchmark_audit/excels_MR_task/selected_mathematical_reasoning_{0015,0117,0126}.xlsx, which hold exactly the 110/120/102 = 332 FinMR practice cases with message, gold, input and segmentation_path; agentic_benchmark_audit/constructMR2HF.ipynb (builds the HF dataset); and select_usgaap_segmentation.ipynb (builds the taxonomy section). The code that cuts a filing into statement-level sub-filings is NOT in the repo.

WHERE THE FINDINGS CAME FROM. Paper section 3.2.1 (paper.txt l.300-307): 4,545 official DQC error messages for 372 companies, 2020-2024, collected 'via the XBRL US portal' (footnote: xbrl.us/data-quality/filing-results). The CSV columns are exactly the XBRL US API assertion fields: assertion.code, assertion.detail, assertion.run-date, entity.cik, report.accession, report.sec-url, report.entry-url, report.filing-year, plus folder_name. Filings were then fetched from EDGAR via report.sec-url (section 3.2.2). DQC was not re-run with Arelle locally: assertion.detail is the XBRL US processor log line, e.g. '2022-01-14 17:30:24,842 [DQC.US.0015.1964] ... Rule version: 16.0.10 - plasma-20211130_10q.htm 736'.

HOW GOLD IS DERIVED. gpt-4.1-mini (the paper says GPT-4o-mini) parses each message into JSON (0015 nb cells 12-14, 0117 cell 12, 0126 system prompt). 0015: extracted = the message's 'has a value of X'; calculated = |X|; question tag and period come from the message's 'Period :' field (0015 nb cell 6 builds answers from res['error_tags'] reported_value / correct_value). 0117: extracted = 'with a value of X'; calculated = 'not equal to the dimensional breakdown of Y'. 0126: extracted = the 'Total Value :' field; calculated = 'The sum of these child components is Y'. I checked this by regex over all 332 selected rows (/tmp/claude-1000/finaud/gold_vs_msg.py): gold equals the message values in 331/332 cases. The one mismatch is an LLM transcription error: 0126 OtherOperatingIncomeExpenseNet has gold 320002 where the message says 32,002. Gold keeps the message's comma formatting, though the LLM sometimes drops commas (message -1,284 became gold '-1284').

QUESTION TEXT. The questions are templated straight from the parsed tag and period (constructMR2HF cells 11-13): "What's the reported value of {tag} in the Instance document for the period {period}?" and "What's the actual value of {tag} ... calculated based on the calculation relationship?". The message's Dimensions field and the statement name are NOT carried into the question.

NO DEDUPLICATION IN PRACTICE. Every message became a case. In the 0015 practice set, 62/110 flagged facts are dimensional (the message's 'Dimensions :' is non-empty), and the 110 cases cover only 86 distinct (filing, concept, period) keys. Across all rules, public_dev.jsonl has 21 groups (58 cases) of byte-identical queries, e.g. DEV_000003-000006, whose golds can differ. Example: 10k-noc-20221231 DefinedBenefitPlanBenefitObligationBenefitsPaid 2021 has two cases with gold -157,000,000 (OtherPostretirement member) and -1,964,000,000 (Pension member). 10q-kmx-20221130 has headline -48,000 plus 3 members, each its own case. 0117 has the same problem: 10k-so-20211231 Revenues 2019 has 5 messages from 5 different statements, with calculated 16,991M (x3), 2,907M and 3,792M. The member sum depends on which statement's table the message came from.

DEV/TEST ARE DEDUPLICATED. In development_inputs.jsonl and test_inputs.jsonl there are 0 identical queries. Grouping by (xsd filename stem, Question1) finds only 3 dev and 2 test groups, and those are different Lord Abbett filings that share a filename stem (the predictions differ). So the hidden phases keep at most one case per (filing, concept, period). Which message was kept is not documented anywhere.

MESSAGE ORDER LOOKS ARBITRARY. In the CSV, rows are grouped by concept and ordered by log timestamp within a concept. Compared with the instance, that order does not follow instance-document fact order: kmx messages run Cash, Stock, Others while the instance runs Stock, Others, Cash, and noc messages run Postretirement then Pension against the reverse in the instance. It does not follow Workiva table-cell order either: the kmx fact-id tablerange cells are 5-2 Stock, 5-3 Others, 5-5 Cash. It is not alphabetical by member, and it does not follow source line: bctf message lines are 12654, 12653, 12655 in emitted order. So whether the hidden-set builder kept the first or the last message, the result cannot be predicted from anything in the case.

HOW THE SNIPPET WAS CHOSEN (practice). 0015 (nb cell 6) and 0117 (nb cell 6) walk os.listdir(filing_folder), which is arbitrary filesystem order, over statement sub-filings, and take the FIRST whose instance file contains the tag string (tag, tag without ':', or tag with '_'). 0126 (nb lines 26-37, 53-111) first fuzzy-matches the message's statement name (to_pascal_case) against folder names, then applies the same tag-string test. For 0015 the snippet therefore says nothing about which dimensional fact was flagged.

SNIPPET CONTENT (dev, checked by script). All 680 dev cases contain exactly one presentation role. In 200/200 sampled cases every non-dei concept in the instance appears in that role's presentation linkbase, and no context is unused. Contexts are NOT filtered by the role's dimensions: in 551/584 dev cases with dimensional facts, some fact's axis is absent from the role's presentation. So the instance holds every fact, in every context, for the concepts presented in one role, and does not single out the flagged fact.

THE US GAAP TAXONOMY SECTION is built from the target tag only (select_usgaap_segmentation cell 9: for MR, query = [input['tag']]). It is that tag's core chunk plus its relations chunk, taken from the taxonomy of report.filing-year.

WHERE THE ~32.8k TRUNCATION COMES FROM. Every XML section was stored in .xlsx cells, and Excel caps a cell at 32,767 characters. In the selected xlsx, presentation, definition, label and instance all max out at exactly 32,767; instance is truncated in 75/110 (0015), 70/120 (0117) and 40/102 (0126) cases. This is the 'incomplete filing content' that the 28 Sep 2026 README revision fixed for dev/test.

PRACTICE-ONLY LABEL LEAK. In all 120 practice 0117 cases the '##Schema document' section is 'None', because of a bug in the 0117 notebook (sch=read_xml(...) where temp_sch was intended). 0015 and 0126 have an XSD. All 680 dev and 680 test cases have an XSD, so the hidden sets were built with a corrected pipeline.

0126 ONLY FLAGS THE CURRENT PERIOD. The message says 'values reported ... in the current reporting period of ...'. In practice, the question's period end equals the document date (folder_name date) in 102/102 cases, with durations Q 12, H 11, 9M 42, Y 25, plus 12 instants. 0015 and 0117 flag prior periods often: 50/110 and 69/120 have period end different from the document end.

0117 MESSAGE SEMANTICS. 'This rule takes the dimensional values of an axis reported on the face financial statements and adds them up and compares them to the actual aggregate value reported anywhere in the filing.' The message names the statement and (in newer versions) 'using the dimension <axis> which is comprised of the members ...'. Axes seen in practice: StatementClassOfStockAxis 58, ProductOrServiceAxis 30, RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis 21, StatementBusinessSegmentsAxis 6, LongtermDebtTypeAxis 4, FinancialInstrumentAxis 1. Of the 15 practice 0117 cases with extracted '0', 12 have an explicit reported 0 headline fact and 3 have no non-dimensional fact in the (truncated) snippet. So '0' does not always mean 'not reported', despite what the toolkit README says.

0126 MESSAGE SEMANTICS. The message lists child components with signed weights, zero values included, and says 'The rule will not add dimension components as the financial statement does not include a table'. The gold calculated value is the message's stated sum.

OVERLAP CHECK. The XBRL_Auditing CSVs cover 149 filing stems, and none of them appears in dev or test (0 matches on the xsd stem). The repo is practice-only and cannot be used to look answers up. The same company can recur across phases in a different filing (noc-20221231 in practice, noc-20251231 in dev).

PAPER QUALITY CONTROL (section 3.3.2). 50 filings were checked by hand for segmentation, and 50% of instances were double-checked against human review. Gold is still LLM-transcribed from the messages, so occasional transcription errors remain.
inferred: Dev/test were probably built from a newer pull of XBRL US DQC messages with the same per-rule notebooks. Evidence: dev filings run into 2025 (fcco-20251231, efc-20250930, noc-20251231); the README says '455 companies'; and the schema bug is fixed. The build code for the hidden sets is not public.

The hidden sets' (filing, concept, period) dedup most likely kept one message per key; pandas drop_duplicates keeps the first by default. Since message order looks effectively random (hash or set order inside the XULE processor), the kept fact in an ambiguous 0015 group is close to a uniform draw from the flagged facts. That fits the observed numbers: 19 dev cases predicted as 0015 have more than one distinct negative candidate value, and we have 12 0015 errors (an expected ~11 if we pick 1 of 2-3 at random).

Under 'keep one random message', P(gold value) is proportional to the number of flagged facts carrying that value. So a value carried by several facts (headline plus member with the same amount, or a member plus its parent) is more likely to be gold than a value carried by one. This is the only principled 0015 tiebreak I can derive from the construction. Low-to-moderate confidence.

For 0117 and 0126, the hidden-set builder very likely picked the segment by matching the statement name in the DQC message, as the 0126 notebook does. If so, the single role in each dev query IS the statement the message refers to, and 0117 member sums should be restricted to that role's own hypercube, axis and members. Practice Southern Co shows that a different statement gives a different 0117 sum.

The 3 dev 0117 extraction errors may be cases where DQC's 'aggregate value reported anywhere in the filing' differs from the first non-dimensional fact we pick (duplicate facts with different decimals, nil facts, or a 0 headline). Not verifiable without the messages.
discrepancies_with_our_code: solve.py negative_dim_facts / TIEBREAK='instance' assumes the dataset targets the first negative member in instance-document order. The construction data contradicts this: in every practice group I could check, DQC message order differs from instance order, Workiva table order and alphabetical member order. No observable ordering determines the targeted fact.

solve.py r0015() always prefers the headline whenever the headline is negative (rep<0). In practice, headline and member facts are flagged and kept on equal footing (kmx: headline -48,000 plus 3 members, each its own case). On dev cases with a negative headline and a member with a different value (DEV3_000015/016, 063, 134), the headline is not provably the target. It is only about as likely as any other flagged fact, or more likely if its value is repeated.

decide() can return the 0126 mechanism for targets whose period is not the current reporting period. DQC_0126 cases are current-period only (102/102 in practice, verified). rules.is_current_period / target_is_current exist but are not used to gate 0126 in decide().

member_sums_0117 falls back to statement_members() / m117_any ('0117_nohyper') from any role, but the hidden-set snippet holds exactly one role (verified for 680/680 dev cases). Whatever the member set, it must come from that role's own definition hypercube, so the fallback adds no information beyond the hyper path.
recommended_changes: Gate 0126 on the current period. Read the document period end from the dei:DocumentPeriodEndDate (or DocumentType) context in the instance, falling back to the xsd stem's date (e.g. abc-20250930.xsd gives 2025-09-30). If the target's end or instant differs from it, never return the 0126 mechanism; fall through to 0117/0015. For durations, any of Q, H, 9M or Y may be valid, so only check the END date.

0015 tiebreak, replacing TIEBREAK='instance'. Collect every non-excluded negative fact for concept+period: the headline plus each dimensional fact, counting duplicate facts separately. Group them by numeric value and choose the value with the highest count. Break remaining ties toward the headline, then toward instance order. Only the 19 ambiguous dev cases can change, so A/B it with one dev submission if a slot is free.

Do not hard-prefer the headline when a member with a different value is also negative: apply the same multiplicity rule. A headline counted twice (e.g. DEV3_000015, where -14000 appears on two non-dimensional facts) wins naturally.

When evaluating 0015 logic on the practice set, treat the 21 identical-query groups (58 cases) as multi-label: a prediction matching any gold in its group is correct. Otherwise practice accuracy on 0015 understates true accuracy and gives misleading tuning signals.

For 0117, build the member set only from the single role in the case: the axes declared in that role's hypercube that holds the target, and the members under that axis in the role. Use the extracted value exactly as reported (0 when the headline is a 0 fact or absent). Keep the 'compare against any non-dimensional fact for the period' semantics.

Expect about 0.3% irreducible gold noise: LLM transcription errors such as 320002 vs 32,002 in practice. The judge uses zero tolerance on calculated_value, so stop chasing a case once it reproduces the message's arithmetic.

Do not use the XBRL_Auditing CSVs or XBRL US API messages for dev/test cases. That would be the prohibited 'look the answers up' route under the Terms. The repo is useful only for understanding construction and for practice-set analysis; there is no dev/test overlap in it anyway.
